chapter: Orchestra people and Xavier chamber concerts
title: Chamber music concerts at Xavier University
summary: Violist Cliff Richter persuaded Xavier to host Sunday chamber concerts with about 14 symphony players, which drew packed houses and even Hilsberg; Mazzari likens chamber music to a jazz band.

blocks.x: What about Xavier University? What is that?

Oh, uh, yes, Xavier University. Well, I tell you. Uh... Oh, just about the last year before I left New Orleans, Cliff Richter played viola in the symphony and I was playing bass, of course. And, uh, Cliff was teaching at Xavier and he was a very ardent lover of Bach and chamber music and so on and so forth. And through his efforts, he finally taught a mother, what's her name there, who was in charge of the school, to put on some chamber music, Xavier. And he would guarantee that there, you know, there would be a success. And so finally, I guess, after talking a long time, he began a series of these things. And sure enough, there was a packed house every time. We put these things on on a Sunday afternoon. And they were very enjoyable. And they were, I mean, uh, any musician... And there were stuff with

who plays classical music, dreams of the time when you can play a little chamber music, because actually you're playing one part and you're playing it all along and you're the only guy doing it, and boy, it's just a real kick to hear yourself playing a certain line. Well anyway, these concerts were very, very successful. In fact, so successful that Alexander Hillsburg attended them, at least one of them, you know, and that was quite a thing to drag him out of there. He usually doesn't go and listens to very many things, but these were very, very good. And you know, chamber music, the old days actually has something to do with the jazz of today. You know, there are so many men in a group, and each man has something to play differently. It's the same thing like a jazz band, you know. It's chamber music, that's what it is. Sure.
How many men did you have out there?
Well, it varied. It'd be about 14 men on the stage.
